articles.title: Systematic reviews and the needs of the adolescent transgender health care field.
articles.population: Adolescents who are transgender, gender diverse, or non-binary (aged from start of puberty to 18 years)
articles.outcomes: Psychosocial, cognitive, and physical outcomes of pubertal suppression and gender-affirming hormone therapy
articles.take_home: This analysis examined 13 existing systematic reviews on gender-affirming treatments for adolescents and found they are being misused to influence treatment decisions. The authors emphasise that clinical guidelines should combine empirical evidence with clinical expertise and patient values, not rely on reviews alone.

articles.title: Benefits and complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis of serial casting in early onset scoliosis.
articles.authors: Sharma S, Ramnarine A, Fouad K, Cheung A, Khurana V, Sankar S, et al.
articles.outcomes: Treatment-related complications, Cobb angle correction, thoracic height progression, pulmonary function, quality of life
articles.take_home: Serial casting is a safe and effective treatment for early-onset scoliosis, with a complication rate of 17% mostly involving minor skin problems that improve after treatment. It preserves spinal growth and produces results comparable to or better than other treatments like bracing, whilst allowing the spine to continue growing.

articles.title: Is Susceptibility to Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis Linked to Obesity-Associated Proximal Femoral Morphology?
articles.authors: Wu J, Zhang D, Canavese F, Li M, Li L
articles.study_type: Comparative cross-sectional and retrospective cohort study
articles.population: Obese and normal-weight children aged 6 to 15 years; retrospective SCFE cohort from 2011 to 2025
articles.sample_size: 42 obese children and 42 normal-weight controls in first group; SCFE cohort size not specified
articles.outcomes: Proximal femoral morphology measurements (femoral head diameter, epiphyseal cupping ratio, Alsberg angle, posterior sloping angle); skeletal maturity; age at SCFE onset
articles.take_home: Obese children develop skeletal maturity about a year earlier than normal-weight children, but the increased risk of slipped capital femoral epiphysis in obesity is not caused by differences in hip bone shape. The risk is more likely due to extra body weight itself rather than how the hip bones are formed.

articles.title: Radiological and clinical outcomes following pelvic support osteotomy with limb length equalization in children.
articles.authors: Ethanur Thuppale V, Arikrishnan A, Reddy J, Gahukamble A, Palocaren T
articles.population: Children with severe post-septic hip sequelae and limb length discrepancy
articles.outcomes: Radiological remodeling of osteotomy angle and Harris Hip functional scores
articles.take_home: Pelvic support osteotomy combined with limb length procedures improved hip function significantly (Harris Hip scores rose from 58 to 89 at 2 years), but the bones remodelled considerably after surgery, particularly in younger children, which may require repeat operations in the future.

articles.title: Subaxial Cervical Spine Injuries in Children: Do Adult Classification Systems Help With Surgical Decision-Making?
articles.authors: Paulson AE, La Poche A, Montgomery A, Metcalf T, Vittetoe K, Benvenuti T, et al.
articles.population: Children younger than 18 years with acute traumatic subaxial cervical spine injuries
articles.outcomes: Validity of SLIC classification system in predicting need for surgery versus non-operative treatment, using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and area under the curve
articles.take_home: The adult SLIC classification system works reasonably well in older children for identifying serious cervical spine injuries, but tends to recommend unnecessary surgery in children under 10 years old. The study suggests SLIC should be used carefully in younger children and that further research is needed to develop age-specific guidelines.

articles.title: Defining Postoperative Weight Trends in Pediatric Patients Undergoing Limb Reconstruction Surgery by Distraction Osteogenesis.
articles.authors: Yalcinkaya A, Sepas A, Yong B, Bafor A, Iobst C
articles.population: Children undergoing limb reconstruction surgery by distraction osteogenesis
articles.sample_size: 175 patients across 4 treatment groups with 1066 postoperative weight measurements
articles.outcomes: Postoperative weight change trajectories over 84 days; timing and magnitude of maximum weight loss; association between early weight loss and bone healing index
articles.take_home: Children undergoing limb lengthening surgery typically lose weight in the first 6 weeks after surgery, with the greatest weight loss (about 2% below baseline) occurring around 45 days, followed by gradual recovery. Those who had intramedullary lengthening showed the most pronounced weight decline and recovery pattern.

articles.title: Temporary in Situ Pinning With Subsequent Modified Dunn is a Safe Alternative to Primary Modified Dunn in Moderate and Severe Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis.
articles.authors: Adams J, Zalneraitis B, Whiting G, Pahlau R, Carry P, De S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with moderate to severe slipped capital femoral epiphysis
articles.sample_size: 29 patients (12 in temporary in situ pinning with subsequent modified Dunn group, 17 in primary modified Dunn group)
articles.outcomes: Complication rates including avascular necrosis, Merle d'Aubigne scores, radiographic morphologic parameters and signs of osteoarthritis
articles.take_home: Temporary pinning followed by modified Dunn surgery was as safe as doing modified Dunn surgery straightaway, with similar complication rates and hip function scores. This staged approach may be useful when an experienced hip surgeon is not immediately available.
